text: {"question":"How does the inclusion of the Planck prior on the Hubble constant affect the statistical preference for screened fifth‑force models compared to the baseline ΛCDM fit, and what change is observed when TRGB distances are added to the calibration?","reference_answer":"Adding the Planck H0 prior eliminates any statistically acceptable compromise for most screened models, keeping ΔBIC negative; only the Φ–screening model with Rmax = 0.4 Mpc achieves a positive ΔBIC (+9.5). However, once TRGB distances are incorporated, this support weakens and the evidence becomes mixed across the TRGB datasets, with no strong preference remaining."}
